data.narrative:
Kneron, a Series B semiconductor company, is valued against a peer set of 4 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies (SambaNova Systems, d-Matrix, Positron AI, DEEPX) spanning $529M to $11.0B. The comp universe also includes 3 public semiconductor benchmarks (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) with a median P/S of 21.0x, though public-comp anchoring is not applicable due to unavailable revenue data for the target.

Two valuation methods triangulate to a range. Stage-progression, using the $190M total raised as a base proxy and applying a 1.9x Series B step-up multiplier, implies $361M. Peer-median valuation across the 4 same-sector comparables yields $1.5B, materially higher and reflecting the volatility in this cohort—the peer range spans nearly 21x from floor to ceiling. These two methods produce a low estimate of $307M, median of $930M, and high of $1.7B.

The wide spread reflects genuine uncertainty in early-stage semiconductor valuations. The $1.2B gap between stage-progression and peer-median suggests either that Kneron trades at a discount to its peer cohort or that the peer set exhibits outsized hype valuations. Without revenue visibility, profitability metrics, or IP/patent differentiation data, the median point of $930M should be treated as indicative rather than precise. Key downside risks include funding environment contraction and competitive pressure from well-capitalized incumbents.
